classification.difficultyReason: Development: direct readings and midpoint interpolation lead to a reverse estimate at 14 cm that is not a midpoint. The hardest demand is locating that height on the correct segment and projecting to the day axis, applying the taught graphical procedure without a new insight.

content.prompt: Consider the line graph to the right.

spec.description: Dashed polyline from the unmarked origin through five blue cross markers; rectangular grey grid and positive-axis arrows.
spec.mathematics: Readings (2,3), (4,6), (6,10), (8,17), (10,18). Horizontal grid interval 1 day; vertical grid interval 2 cm. These are sampled observations, not a function supplied by an equation.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph; no answer annotations.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How tall was the grass on day 4?

answer.worked: At day 4, the plotted point has height $6\text{ cm}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: On what day did the grass reach 10 cm?

answer.worked: Read across from $10\text{ cm}$ to the plotted point, then down to the day axis: day 6.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Estimate the height of the grass on day 3.

answer.worked: Day 3 is halfway between days 2 and 4. The line is halfway between $3\text{ cm}$ and $6\text{ cm}$, giving an estimated height of $4.5\text{ cm}$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Estimate when the grass reached 14 cm.

answer.short: Approximately day 7; about day 7.1 is also acceptable.
answer.worked: Read across from $14\text{ cm}$ to the dashed segment, then down to the day axis. The intersection is just after day 7, approximately day 7.1, or day 7 to the nearest day.
